definitions.explanation: A place to put one's foot when climbing or a secure position from which to advance.
Something that helps one make progress or achieve a goal figuratively.

examples.japanese: {岩|いわ}の{足掛|あしが}かりを{探|さが}す。
examples.english: To look for a foothold on the rock.

examples.japanese: {崖|がけ}を{登|のぼ}るには{足掛|あしが}かりが{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: You need footholds to climb the cliff.

examples.japanese: この{資格|しかく}を{足掛|あしが}かりにキャリアアップを{目指|めざ}す。
examples.english: I aim to advance my career using this qualification as a stepping stone.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{成功|せいこう}を{足掛|あしが}かりに、さらに{飛躍|ひやく}したい。
examples.english: I want to use this success as a springboard to achieve even more.

examples.japanese: インターンシップは{就職|しゅうしょく}への{足掛|あしが}かりになる。
examples.english: Internships serve as a stepping stone to employment.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{進出|しんしゅつ}の{足掛|あしが}かりとして、まず{現地|げんち}{法人|ほうじん}を{設立|せつりつ}した。
examples.english: As a foothold for overseas expansion, we first established a local subsidiary.

notes:
{足掛|あしが}かり can be physical or figurative.

WRITING:
Also written as {足がかり} or {足懸|あしが}かり.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {足掛|あしが}かりになる: to serve as a stepping stone
- {足掛|あしが}かりにする: to use as a stepping stone
- {足掛|あしが}かりを{得|え}る: to gain a foothold
- {足掛|あしが}かりを{築|きず}く: to establish a foothold

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {手掛|てが}かり: handhold; clue
- {足場|あしば}: scaffolding; footing
